subject: Capacity commitment clarification & test slate — next steps
messages:
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@nimbusdiag.com>
Cc: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: capacity commitments, fallback policy & proposed test slate

Hi Sara — great to meet today, and thanks for sharing the production goals. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so nothing falls through the cracks.

Summary from today's call
- Primary ask: predictable inference throughput for Q4 rollout — target 300 tokens/s sustained across 6 concurrent workers for top-10 endpoints.
- Constraint: must have a capacity guarantee (reserved pool or equivalent) with clear fallbacks if we hit spikes.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer committed monthly pricing but need clarity on burst-to-cloud economics and any hidden egress/replication fees.

Redwood differentiators (call highlights)
- Dedicated pools with SLA-backed latency/availability and configurable burst policy to hyperscaler when needed.
- Smart routing that prefers reserved capacity by default and fails over to verified model variants on other infra to protect SLOs.
- Unit-cost controls: batching + KV cache + quantization profiles that reduce per-token cost without manual infra changes.

Proposed test slate (asks we agreed to):
1) Sustained throughput run (48 hours): reserve a Dedicated pool sized to 350 tokens/s headroom and run canonical queries (you'll provide the top-10 endpoints and P95 target). We log latency, token-cost, and tail behavior.
2) Spike/fallover test: simulate 3x traffic bursts and validate automated fallback to cloud burst path + model variant. Confirm end-to-end request success rate and mean failover latency.
3) Failure injection: disconnect a dedicated node and validate auto-routing and instance replacement behavior under load.
4) Cost delta workbook: we'll run identical traces on (a) your preferred hyperscaler reserved VMs (you provide config) and (b) Redwood Dedicated to produce a normalized $/1000 tokens calc.

Attachments: I've attached a short comparison matrix and the demo logs we captured.

Next steps and owners
- Sara: share top-10 endpoints + representative traces, and your preferred hyperscaler VM/commit config by EOW (Jun 17).
- Aisha: draft Dedicated pool sizing + RB/SC (routing/backfill) policy and baseline cost estimates (delivery Jun 15).
- Rishi: propose a compact test harness we can run on both sides and capture the metrics we need (Jun 12).
- Jonas (me): coordinate dates for the 48-hour run and produce the side-by-side workbook.

Would suggest we lock the 48-hour run window for Jun 22-24 if that still works for your launch timeline.

Thanks — we think there's a clear path to give you the commitment semantics you need while keeping a measurable cost delta to hyperscalers.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: capacity commitments, fallback policy & proposed test slate (internal)

Jonas / Rishi — quick internal sync before we send the test plan to Nimbus. Key notes and my proposed numbers: 

Sizing proposal (initial)
- Baseline: target sustained 300 tokens/s across 6 workers -> effective 50 tokens/s per worker.
- Buffer: provision 350 tokens/s (≈ +17%) for the Dedicated pool to avoid immediate autoscale pressure during steady state.
- KV cache: allocate 40% cache hit expected from the traces Sara sent — this reduces both latency and token compute; we'll validate during the 48h run.

Fallback and RTO expectations
- Warm-standby routing to hyperscaler pool: typical failover detection + routing completes in ~45–90s depending on active KV warming. Real-world RTO can be ~2–3 min until caches rehydrate for P95-level latencies. Call that our conservative SLO unless we design an active replicated cache.

Test harness and metrics
- Rishi: let's capture per-request: timestamp, route (dedicated/hs), model-variant, latency p50/p95/p99, token_count, error_code. We'll calculate $/1k tokens using GPU-hours + reserved amortization assumptions.

Costs and workbook inputs (what we need from Nimbus)
- Reserved VM SKU + monthly commit cost and any storage/egress assumptions.
- Expected steady-state Q4 concurrency profile and monthly token volume for normalization.

Action items (internal owners)
- Rishi: draft the harness repo and a small wrapper that runs the same trace against both endpoints (deadline Jun 15).
- Jonas: hold the customer date proposal (Jun 22-24) until we get the traces + SKU.
- Aisha: populate the cost workbook template with planned Dedicated pool assumptions and quantization toggles (Jun 15).

I'll push a short technical appendix to the shared Drive after Rishi drops the harness.

— Aisha
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Sara / Mike — thanks for the quick replies and for committing to the SKU + traces this week. Consolidated next steps and the exact artifacts we'll deliver so we can sign one run order quickly: 

Deliverables from Redwood (what you'll get)
- A 48-hour dedicated-run execution plan (runbook + monitoring dashboard).
- Test harness + instructions to execute the same trace against Nimbus's reserved VM endpoint and Redwood Dedicated.
- Cost workbook with amortized reserved-VPU cost, burst delta, and quantization sensitivity (FP16 vs 8-bit).
- Failure injection script and a summarized RTO/RPO appendix from our last three customer runs.

Customer deliverables we need this week
- Top-10 endpoint traces (sanitized) and a sample steady-state window (preferred format: JSONL).
- Reserved VM SKU + monthly commit and any expected egress/storage fees.
- Point of contact for infra during the 48h run (ops pager or Slack handle).

Sign-off path & timeline
- If we receive artifacts by EOD Jun 17, Redwood will finalize the runbook by Jun 19 and propose the Jun 22-24 window.
- Post-run, we will provide a side-by-side workbook and an executive one-pager for Nimbus procurement.

Legal/contract note: Mike — you mentioned Nimbus prefers a 12-month reservation. We can draft an addendum that mirrors the Dedicated commit semantics with a fallback cap for burst usage; I'll loop Legal once Nimbus confirms term length. There's a DocuSign form we can pre-populate after scope is locked: https://www.docusign.com/forms/XYZ-commitment-v1

Let me know if you'd like a brief 30-min alignment call before the run — happy to host.

Thanks,
Jonas
